title: Why progress tracking was not displayed in csm-orchestrate cycle 6 despite the cycle-5 fix
question: Zero progress tracking was displayed during csm-orchestrate run run-renderer-wiring-r1 (quality delivery cycle 6) despite cycle 5 (run-progress-visibility-r3) supposedly fixing progress tracking. Establish exactly what the driver prints during a run, under what conditions the final TASK PROGRESS projection renders, and why an operator could see no progress tracking.

tl: The user is right: cycle 5 fixed the progress-rendering plumbing but not meaningful progress display. In run-renderer-wiring-r1 the TASK PROGRESS bar moved only in three coarse jumps (0->33->67->100%) and sat frozen at 67% for 44.9s = 92.7% of the run while the largest phase executed, because percentages derive solely from item completion, child skill-progress rollups are provably unable to move the bar (clamp + reset ordering), and nothing during child execution emits updates. Nothing human-readable persists the progress trajectory (it survives only as 26 sqlite WAL snapshot records). One new defect was found: every skill-progress-rollup telemetry event is silently discarded because the event type is unregistered. All findings carry an honest limit: operator stdout was never captured, so "zero displayed" rests on the operator report plus code-path inference.
executiveSummary:
The research question challenged the cycle-5 fix (run-progress-visibility-r3, commit d639baf). A STANDARD-tier, local-mode pipeline ran three parallel read-only researchers (runtime rendering path; progress semantics; captured run evidence), an anti-anchored challenger, and an independent judge. Outcome: the cycle-5 plumbing claims held (live onProgress prints fire; the terminal receipt is unconditionally keyed so result.progress is non-null and the final projection guard passes) — but the displayed result was still not meaningful progress.



Strongest evidence: the run cursor.db-wal persists 26 distinct progress-snapshot revisions showing plannedProgress moved exactly three times — 0 -> 0.333 at 06:03:34.857, -> 0.667 at 06:03:37.945, -> 1 at 06:04:22.831 — so the bar was frozen at 67% for 44.88s, 92.7% of the 48.4s run. The telemetry timeline corroborates a 44.873s gap with no events. Headline caveats: stdout was never captured (the operator-experience claim is inference; --quiet-progress is unexcludable from artifacts), and the judge initially failed the run because the synthesized draft was never written back into the document — remediated.

keyFindings.claim: The cycle-5 fix shipped functioning rendering plumbing: the tracker onUpdate fires via change() and observeTelemetry(), the driver prints projectProgress text live through onProgress, and the terminal receipt is keyed into progressByReceipt before the telemetry-loss early return, so result.progress is non-null and the final projection guard passes in every healthy run.

Display showed no meaningful movement: the bar moved only at phase completions (0->33->67->100%) and sat frozen at 67% for 44.88s = 92.7% of the 48.4s run while the largest phase executed, because plannedProgress sums weight x verifiedFraction, active items hold fraction 0, and only the phase-end transition forces fraction 1.

Child skill-progress rollups can never move the bar: the shipped recorder writes overallPercent 100 only after the child completes, the post-invocation per-node update resets verifiedFraction, and updateProgress clamps fraction 1 back to 0 on any non-verified item — so rollups add an evidenceRef but structurally cannot change the percentage.

A 44.873-second silent dead zone covered 92.7% of the run: the child executes inside one awaited invocation race with no per-milestone hooks, and telemetry emits nothing between dispatch and review, so no tracker update or render occurs during real phase work.

Rendering is an appended block per notification with byte-identical text for consecutive telemetry-only updates (only JSON revision/eventsObserved differ), so live output was a few frozen snapshots separated by silence rather than a moving display.

No human-readable artifact evidences progress for the run: receipt.json has no progress key, the receipt.md/html render profile excludes progress by design, stdout was never captured, and telemetry has no progress event type — the full trajectory survives only as 26 distinct progress-snapshot records in cursor.db-wal, unretrievable without sqlite tooling.

Cycle-5 verification could not catch the defect: the only driver-level test asserts stdout contains TASK PROGRESS/Milestones — satisfiable by the first pending-state print alone — and no test asserts the rendered percentage moves during a run or that the final projection renders distinctly.

NEW DEFECT: every skill-progress-rollup telemetry event is silently discarded — skill-progress-rollup is absent from TELEMETRY_EVENT_TYPES, emit() throws for unlisted types, and the rollup site bare catch swallows the throw; run-renderer-wiring-r1 fired 3 rollups (persisted evidenceRefs prove it) yet telemetry.jsonl contains zero rollup events. Fix candidate: register the event type.

detailSections:
## The corrected bar trajectory

The persisted WAL snapshots (26 distinct revisions, deduplicated by revision; ~90 raw WAL frame occurrences) record plannedProgress moving exactly three times: 0 -> 0.333 at 06:03:34.857Z (p1 complete), -> 0.667 at 06:03:37.945Z (p2 complete), -> 1 at 06:04:22.831Z (p3 complete). The bar therefore sat frozen at 67% from 06:03:37.945 to 06:04:22.828 — 44.88s, 92.7% of the 48.4s run — during the very phase (the battery + capture verification) an operator most wanted visibility into.

## Why the cycle-5 fix could not display movement

1. Aggregate math: plannedProgress = sum(weight x verifiedFraction) / sum(weight). Dispatch sets state active but leaves verifiedFraction at 0; nothing contributes until verified.
2. The clamp: updateProgress forces verifiedFraction to 1 on verified and resets fraction 1 to 0 on any non-verified state. A child record with overallPercent 100 rolled onto an active item is therefore clamped straight back to 0.
3. The ordering: the post-invocation per-node update deliberately resets evidenceRefs/fraction before the rollup runs (the cycle-5 ordering fix guarantees the rollup is last writer — and the clamp guarantees it never wins).
4. The dead zone: the child runs inside one awaited Promise.race in the host invocation adapter; no parent-side hook exists between dispatch and the post-child review event.
5. Presentation: each notification console.logs a full block; consecutive telemetry-only snapshots render identical text, so the visible effect is repetition, not movement.

## What was and was not persisted

Persisted: 26 WAL progress snapshots (machine-only), 12 telemetry records (5 event types, no progress events), skill-progress child records (3), receipt.json/md/html (progress excluded by profile). Not persisted: stdout, the invocation command, any human-readable progress trajectory. The plan journal cycle-5 row (sequence 17) claims the run printed live milestone rows — an ephemeral-stdout assertion backed only by the primary in-session tail capture (one milestone row visible in a 4-line tail), not by durable evidence.

## New defect: silently discarded rollup telemetry

telemetry.mjs TELEMETRY_EVENT_TYPES does not include skill-progress-rollup; emit() throws TypeError for unlisted types; index.mjs wraps the rollup telemetry in a bare catch and swallows it. Three rollups fired in run-renderer-wiring-r1 (their evidenceRefs persisted in the WAL snapshots at revisions 5, 12, 19) yet telemetry.jsonl records zero rollup events. One-line fix candidate: add the type to TELEMETRY_EVENT_TYPES.
recommendation:
Treat the cycle-5 fix as plumbing-complete but display-incomplete. Decision-ready directions (each independently valuable; none authorizes work by itself):

1. RECOMMEND: make the displayed percentage able to move mid-phase — either record partial child skill-progress records (0 < overallPercent < 100) during host work and rework the clamp at progress.mjs:296-297 so rollup-driven fractions on active items survive, or add a heartbeat update sourced from the host. Validation measure: a rendered-percentage-movement test asserting strictly increasing rendered percentages across a run.
2. RECOMMEND: persist a human-readable progress.json (final snapshot) into each run evidence dir — the trajectory already exists in the WAL; it just needs a readable projection. Validation: evidence-dir inventory check per run.
3. RECOMMEND: fix the rollup telemetry discard by registering skill-progress-rollup in TELEMETRY_EVENT_TYPES; validate by asserting rollup events appear in telemetry.jsonl.
4. CONSIDER: render only on visible text change (hash the text, skip identical blocks) or use an in-place TTY update, so repeated snapshots do not read as spam.
5. AVOID: claiming progress-tracking completion from substring stdout assertions; require percentage-movement and final-render-distinctness assertions instead.

What would change the recommendation: if partial child records prove infeasible for real hosts (e.g. hosts cannot report incremental state honestly), option 1 should fall back to phase-level coarseness made explicit in the projection (show per-phase expected duration or a spinner state) rather than a misleading frozen percentage.
